title: Underestimating Distributed Counter Read Error
pattern: Naively summing thread-local counters sequentially to obtain a global total and assuming the read error is zero.
why_bad: Because the counter summation is not instantaneous and consumes time ($\Delta$), and concurrent threads continue to increment at rate ($r$), the values are read out-of-sync. The mathematically expected error in the total count read is $r\Delta / 2$. Failing to account for this error can lead to system bugs if invariants rely on absolute exact values.
detection: Sequential non-synchronized iterations over thread-local counters used for logic checks rather than raw diagnostic stats.
counterexample: Valid if the system is fully paused during read, or if absolute precision is not required (e.g., purely statistical counters).
fix: Accept that the count is an approximation, or use synchronized read sweeps if exactness is required.
strength: Strong` — mathematically demonstrates a non-zero read error bounded by $r\Delta / 2$.
source: *1701.00854v6.pdf*, Answer to Quick Quiz 5.17, Appendix E, p. 492.
